faq.heading: Frequently asked questions
faq.sub: Everything you need to know about Takt Studio and line simulation

items.q: How accurate are Takt Studio's calculations?
items.a: Calculations are based on standard Industrial Organization Engineering formulas. Accuracy depends on the quality of input data (cycle times, efficiencies). It is an analytical simulation tool for decision-making, not a real-time control system.

items.q: Where is my simulation data stored?
items.a: For privacy and security, your data never leaves your device. It is stored in your browser's local storage (localStorage). If you clear your cache or switch browsers, data will not sync unless you export it manually.

items.q: Can I export my analyses to other formats?
items.a: Yes, Takt Studio lets you export results and the current configuration as PDF for presentations and technical reports, as well as import/export JSON files to share models between users.

items.q: Do I need advanced Lean Manufacturing knowledge?
items.a: Not required, but it helps. The tool is designed to be intuitive, but concepts like 'Bottleneck' or 'Line Balancing' are fundamental to correctly interpret results and make improvement decisions.

metodologia.title: Methodology and model assumptions
metodologia.subtitle: How Takt Studio calculates its metrics and the limitations of the analytical model.
metodologia.introP1: Takt Studio is a deterministic analytical model of industrialized production lines. It uses cycle times, number of operators, demand and shifts to calculate key operational metrics: takt time, throughput, lead time and balancing efficiency.
metodologia.introP2: The tool is neither a full discrete event simulation (DES) nor a definitive financial validation. Its value lies in pre-validating improvement decisions before intervening on the shop floor, providing a fast and rigorous first quantitative approximation.
metodologia.introWarning: Results are indicative. For real investment decisions, they must be calibrated with real operational and financial data from the line.

kpiCards.title: Takt Time
kpiCards.p: The rate at which you must produce to meet demand. It expresses the maximum allowed time per unit.
kpiCards.note: A low takt time indicates aggressive demand; a high takt time, relaxed demand.

kpiCards.title: Effective cycle time
kpiCards.p: The real time a station consumes per unit, considering parallel operators and rework rate.
kpiCards.note: More operators reduce effective time; more failures increase it through inherent rework.

kpiCards.title: Bottleneck
kpiCards.p: The station that limits the overall line rate: the one with the highest effective cycle time.
kpiCards.note: Relieving the bottleneck is the highest-impact action on overall throughput.

kpiCards.title: Throughput
kpiCards.p: Maximum units the line can produce per day, limited by the bottleneck.
kpiCards.note: Throughput never exceeds the bottleneck's capacity, regardless of the performance of the other stations.

kpiCards.title: Lead Time
kpiCards.p: Estimated total time for a unit to travel the entire line from entry to exit.
kpiCards.note: It does not model queues or buffer waits; it approximates pure travel time.

kpiCards.title: Balancing efficiency
kpiCards.p: A measure of how balanced effective times are across stations.
kpiCards.note: A value of 1.0 indicates a perfectly balanced line. Values below 0.7 suggest an opportunity to redistribute workloads.

metodologia.econIntro: Takt Studio's economic layer translates operational metrics into financial impact estimates under scenario-configurable assumptions.
metodologia.proxyText: The difference between the contribution generated by served units and the total daily operating cost.
metodologia.impactText: For each proposed improvement action, the estimated change in contribution minus the change in operating costs is calculated.
metodologia.paybackText: If the recommendation involves a one-off initial investment (method or quality improvement), the recovery time is estimated.
metodologia.econWarning: The economic layer is an indicative estimate under configurable assumptions. It does not replace a detailed financial analysis or the company's real accounting validation.

limits.label: Deterministic model
limits.text: The calculation is analytical and does not model stochastic cycle time variability, absences or random failures.

limits.label: No full DES
limits.text: It is not a discrete event simulation (DES). It does not model queues, buffers or WIP accumulation between stations.

limits.label: No complex sequencing
limits.text: It does not model alternative routings, complex parallelism or sequence dependencies between stations.

limits.label: Approximate bottleneck
limits.text: The bottleneck is identified as the station with the highest effective cycle time. In reality, the constraint may also depend on WIP policies, staggered shifts or materials.

limits.label: Indicative economic layer
limits.text: Costs, margins and impacts are configurable estimates. They must be calibrated with real accounting and operational data before being used for investment decisions.

limits.label: Simplified lead time
limits.text: Lead time is the sum of effective times. It does not include queue waiting times or transport times between stations.

metodologia.noteP1: Takt Studio's value lies in offering a fast and consistent first quantitative approximation to pre-validate improvement decisions before intervening on the real line. It allows discarding unviable options, prioritizing interventions with the greatest operational impact and backing proposals with numbers.
metodologia.noteP2: For real investment, plant reorganization or hiring decisions, Takt Studio results should be complemented with:
noteItems: In-situ operational validation (direct observation, time studies)
Detailed financial analysis with real accounting data
DES simulation if line complexity justifies it
Judgment of the engineering team and production management
